clue.text: Loaded on shelf, no Time Out

indicators.note: 'no' says the letter for time is to be taken away from the shelf-loading word

parts.note: goods loaded onto a shelf are stacked

explanation.surface: A complaint about a shelf crammed full with no break allowed: a shop worker's grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time Out' looks like a break in sport, but 'Out' is the definition, as in dismissed from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fired from a job is out of work, dismissed by the employer.

clue.text: Pole kicks off, netting first

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, so one piece is held within the other
'off' suggests the letters of kicks have gone wrong, so they are rearranged

parts.note: 1ST, written IST, is the usual short form of first

explanation.surface: A football picture: a shot that strikes the post before finding the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges KICKS and 'netting' holds 1ST (written IST) inside. 'Pole' is not a Polish person but a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier pushes with a stick, which is a kind of pole held in each hand.

clue.text: A vehicle to accommodate theatrical Queen with lead role

parts.note: camp means showy and theatrical in manner
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
the van, short for vanguard, is the leading position

explanation.surface: A touring theatre company finding a van big enough for a flamboyant star.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one vehicle carrying a star; in fact 'A vehicle to accommodate' is the definition and the rest builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorhome is a vehicle fitted out for sleeping and living in, so it gives accommodation.

clue.text: Nelson's whirlpool?

definitions.meaning: Nelson's surname: the American singer and film actor Nelson ..., famous in 1930s musicals
a small swirl of water moving against the main current

explanation.surface: It suggests Admiral Nelson caught in a vortex at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the admiral: Nelson is the singer Nelson Eddy, so the surname answers both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirling current of water is a little whirlpool, and the singer's surname is the same word.

clue.text: Nice getting heated by this

parts.note: Nice is the city on the French Riviera, warmed by a hot wind blowing across the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: It looks like a pleasant thing to be warmed by: 'nice' as an adjective.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised at the start, 'Nice' seems to be the adjective; it is the French city.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot dusty wind from North Africa blows over the Mediterranean to southern Europe, warming places such as Nice.

clue.text: Forced out CEO; credibility shot

indicators.note: 'out' says the letters come out of their order and are rearranged

parts.note: credibility cut short, shot down to its slang form, is cred

explanation.surface: A boardroom coup: the chief executive pushed out once his reputation is in tatters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be coerced is to be compelled or pressured into something, the same as being forced.

clue.text: 1% is collected — they get it

indicators.note: 'collected' means gathered up together and reassembled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
the % sign reads 'per cent'

explanation.surface: A tax or fee: one per cent is taken, and somebody receives it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the symbols as words: 1 is I and % is PERCENT; with IS, those ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who receive something are the people who get it.

clue.text: Homer, an American soldier, is a member of the Royal Household

definitions.text: a member of the Royal Household

parts.note: a homer is an ancient Hebrew measure of capacity, also called a cor
GI is the usual term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson as a US soldier somehow working at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' is not the poet or Simpson but an old Hebrew unit of measure, also called a cor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen's Welsh dogs were famously part of royal life, so one is a household member.

clue.text: on the periodic table

parts.note: the clue's own number, 8, is to be read in front of these words: element number 8 in the chemists' chart

explanation.surface: A clue that starts with its own number: '8 on the periodic table'.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue number is part of the clue: the eighth element of the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Element number eight in the chemical table is the gas we breathe, symbol O.

clue.text: Working girl out of bed for pimp

parts.note: a tart is slang for a prostitute, a euphemistic 'working girl'
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A seedy street picture: a prostitute rising, and her pimp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pimp' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb: to dress up showily.
explanation.definitionFit: To pimp a car or room is to decorate it flashily, much as one might smarten something cheaply.

clue.text: Knut's to act as go-between without delay

parts.note: Knut is the setter, so 'Knut's' is 'I am', shortened to I'M
to mediate is to act as an intermediary between parties

explanation.surface: The setter volunteers to be a go-between at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; 'Knut's' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an action taken instantly, straight away, is done without delay.

clue.text: Crikey! Harry's left town

indicators.note: 'left' says the named man has departed from the exclamation, so his name is removed

parts.note: cor blimey is a Cockney exclamation of surprise, like crikey
Harry Lime is the villain of the film The Third Man

explanation.surface: Shocked surprise at the news that Harry has walked out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry is Harry Lime of The Third Man; take LIME out of the Cockney oath COR BLIMEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Corby is an industrial town in Northamptonshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Drawn, exhausted, disheartened

indicators.note: 'disheartened' means losing its heart, so the central letter of the word for exhausted goes

parts.note: exhausted means very tired

explanation.surface: Three adjectives for a weary, discouraged face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' looks like a third word for haggard, but here it means a game ending level.
explanation.definitionFit: A match that is drawn ends level, with the scores equal.

clue.text: Volatile power company's ticker quote

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and changeable, so the letters are unsettled into a new order

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
CO is company, and the apostrophe-s adds S

explanation.surface: An energy firm's share price swinging wildly on the market ticker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticker quote' reads as one phrase, but 'ticker' is fodder alongside P and COS; only 'quote' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A quote on the market is the price at which shares are currently offered.

clue.text: Fine US traders for manipulation — they're breaking the law

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: manipulation means shifting things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: American traders fined for market manipulation, as criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindlers who cheat people are committing crimes, so they are breaking the law.

clue.text: It's a fraud to insure one of 23's 30

parts.note: to insure something is to cover it against loss
23 is the carmaker and 30 its models; the Up! is one of that maker's small cars

explanation.surface: Insuring one of the carmaker's models turns out to be a fraud, topically in the emissions scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross-references: 23-across is the German carmaker and 30-across is MODELS.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealment of wrongdoing is a deceit, a kind of fraud on the public.

clue.text: I get stuck into Leeds, playing dirty stuff!

indicators.note: to get stuck into is to be pushed inside, so one letter goes inside the other piece
'playing' as in playing up: the letters of the city misbehave and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer getting stuck in against Leeds, who play dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get stuck into' puts I inside DESEL, the letters of LEEDS rearranged by 'playing'.
explanation.definitionFit: This fuel is notorious for sooty, polluting exhaust, so it is dirty stuff.

clue.text: To build up English/American workforce, add mischievous Greek

parts.note: labor, in American spelling, is the workforce
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A plan to expand an Anglo-American workforce by hiring a troublesome Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English/American' hints that the word for workforce is spelt the American way, without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop an idea in more detail is to expand on it, to build it up.

clue.text: Altruistic Santa's beginning without any help

indicators.note: 'beginning' points to the opening letter of the word Santa's

parts.note: Santa's helpers are elves, so with none of them he is elfless

explanation.surface: A generous Santa starting Christmas Eve with no helpers at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'help' ties to Santa: his helpers are elves, so having none is being ELF-LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone altruistic puts others first and thinks little of their own interests.

clue.text: American conscript recorded 22, batting first

indicators.note: 'first' puts the batting word at the front

parts.note: a batsman batting is in

indicators.note: 'recorded' implies a spoken version, so the next word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: 22-down is EVADED, and to evade is to have ducked

explanation.surface: An American draftee who dodged service, batting first in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is cricket's word for at the crease. DUCKED (22-down, EVADED) said aloud gives DUCT.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage, to induct is to enlist a man into the armed forces, to conscript him.

clue.text: A slice of meat ranch exported

indicators.note: 'of' says the slice comes out of these words, taken from within them

explanation.surface: A slab of meat from a ranch, shipped abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A slice of meat' reads as one phrase; only 'A slice' defines, and 'of' signals the letters sitting inside the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice, often of money or shares.

clue.text: Townshend touring Panama could be a bugbear

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Pete Townshend is the guitarist of The Who
a Panama is a brimmed straw hat

explanation.surface: A rock star on tour in Panama, which might annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' is not the country but a straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular dislike that irritates you constantly is a bugbear.

clue.text: Author of The Raven — test some of his other work

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote the poem The Raven
to try is to test

explanation.surface: A suggestion to sample more of Edgar Allan Poe's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe wrote verse besides The Raven, so other works in that form are some of his output.

clue.text: PM rounds on former Labour leader, having performed a 27

indicators.note: 'on' places the reversed name before the Labour leader
'rounds' means turns about, so the PM's name is read backwards

parts.note: Dave is David Cameron, Prime Minister in 2015
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party until 2015

explanation.surface: Prime Minister turning on Ed Miliband after a political sidestep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' turns DAVE (Cameron) into EVAD; 27-across is DODGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have performed a dodge is to have sidestepped or ducked something.

clue.text: With a single ring, Gok Wan loves cooking big fish in hot water

indicators.note: cooking means mixing up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
a ring is the letter O, and keeping a single one means the second O is dropped

explanation.surface: TV stylist Gok Wan loves cooking big fish on a single hob ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Gok Wan is a British TV fashion presenter; 'big fish in hot water' is the carmaker caught in the 2015 emissions scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: The German carmaker, a giant of the industry, was in deep trouble in 2015 over rigged emissions tests.

clue.text: Rich veins, potentially many of them I gather

indicators.note: 'I gather' as in 'I hear', so the word is replaced by one sounding alike

parts.note: loads means many

explanation.surface: A miner talks about promising seams of ore, saying there are many.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit of ore running through rock forms a seam, so these are mineral veins that might be rich.

clue.text: Liechtenstein defensive error turned the game

indicators.note: 'turned' means reversed, so the combined letters read backwards

parts.note: FL is the international vehicle code for Liechtenstein
an OG, own goal, is a defender's error

explanation.surface: A football match turned by a Liechtenstein defender's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses FLOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport, the game played with clubs on a course.

clue.text: Its players need to be up for it!

definitions.text: Its players need to be up for it!

parts.words: Its players need to be up for it!
parts.note: 'up for it' means keen, but the players of this sport must also be up on horseback

explanation.surface: Players must be enthusiastic to play a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is played on horseback, so its players are literally mounted up, as well as needing to be keen.

clue.text: Carmaker's deceitful trick

definitions.meaning: an American car manufacturer, maker of the Viper

explanation.surface: A car company's dishonest scam, topical in the emissions era.
explanation.definitionFit: The American car brand shares its name with a word for a sly ruse or evasion.

clue.text: Firm body!

definitions.meaning: relating to a firm or business company

explanation.definitionFit: The word means belonging to a business and also formed into a single body.

clue.text: The Regiment, outwardly tired, suffering a terrible loss

indicators.note: the anagrammed word sits on the outside, enclosing the regiment
suffering means in a bad way, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the SAS, Special Air Service, is known simply as the Regiment

explanation.surface: Exhausted special forces soldiers taking heavy casualties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges the letters of TIRED, and 'outwardly' makes them wrap the Regiment, the crossword name for the SAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a terrible loss or calamity.

clue.text: They display fashion, large and small

parts.note: a mode is a fashion
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Catwalk figures showing clothes in sizes large and small.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannequins and catwalk walkers show off clothes, so they display them.
